title: A GPT-style chatbot starts by guessing the next word

probes.question: What are GPT-style language models pre-trained to do?
True or false: biased or inaccurate training data can make an LLM's output less reliable.

image.alt: Diagram of the sentence 'Hey Barbora, how are you?' with a target word marked between its left and right context.

body.claim: GPT-style language models are first pre-trained to predict the next word.
body.why: LLMs are neural networks trained on a vast amount of text. GPT-style models are pre-trained to predict the next word, then often fine-tuned to follow instructions and act as assistants. Biased or inaccurate training data can make the output less reliable.
